The Sr-90 measurement of 1500 Bq/L can be viewed a different way. Compare it to potassium, for example. The amount of decaying nuclei per second coming from the potassium in the average human body is ~63Bq/L (based on the average human by volume of 4400Bq per 0.7m^3 for the whole body by volume).

So you already have about 1/20th of the equivalent of Sr-90's radioactivity in you right now. And that's just from the potassium, so unless you're planning on drinking the seawater directly from the plant, there isn't much to worry about.

I knew I'd find a banana argument in here. First off, nearly all potassium ingested is expelled by the kidneys in about 30 days which is why Gatorade is something you consume after each workout and not just once a decade.

Sr-90 however acts like calcium in the body, settling in bones and bone marrow where it sits for on average ~15-20 years before it is expelled. What's more, potassium-40 has a half life over a billion years (not very hot) whereas Sr-90 is around 30 years (dangerously hot).

Essentially then, your argument is akin to comparing dipping your finger in boiling water for a tenth of a second versus dipping it in boiling water for 20 seconds (in terms of biological half-life), and that's not even counting the fact that the water is much hotter in the 2nd scenario since Sr-90 has a far shorter nuclear half-life.

That being the case, I'd rather eat a truckload of bananas than a mere dust particle of Sr-90.
